title: RF vs. Optical Transmission Matrix
subtitle: Detailed physical layer and analog circuit trade-off comparison between Radio Frequency and Optical Assistive Links.

rf.name: Radio Frequency (RF)
pros: Penetrates walls, furniture, and body obstructions
Omnidirectional broad range up to 50+ meters
Seamless roaming across rooms and lecture halls
cons: Susceptible to electromagnetic interference from motors & Wi-Fi

optical.name: Optical (LED–Photodiode)
pros: 100% immune to electromagnetic and RF noise
Confined to room boundaries (inherently secure and private)
Zero RF radiation (safe for medical and MRI zones)
cons: Susceptible to intense direct sunlight / ambient flicker

metrics.rf: Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS). Signals penetrate drywall, wooden partitions, and human bodies.
metrics.optical: Strict Line-of-Sight (LOS) or direct optical reflection required. Blocked by solid objects.

metrics.rf: Medium to Long (15 m – 50+ m) depending on transmitter power and antenna tuning.
metrics.optical: Short to Medium (5 m – 15 m) using high-brightness wide-angle LED arrays.

metrics.rf: Vulnerable to EM fields, fluorescent ballasts, switching power supplies, and Wi-Fi harmonics.
metrics.optical: Completely immune to RF/EM interference. Sensitive only to intense direct ambient sunlight.

metrics.rf: Moderate. Signals bleed through walls, allowing eavesdropping from adjacent spaces without encryption.
metrics.optical: High. Light cannot penetrate opaque walls, creating a physical optical security boundary.

metrics.rf: Auditoriums, open stadiums, large lecture halls, multi-room campus tours.
metrics.optical: Hospitals, MRI/ICU rooms, confidential courtrooms, adjacent classrooms, museum exhibits.

metrics.rf: < 0.1 ms (Pure analog AM carrier, zero DSP buffering delay).
metrics.optical: < 0.1 ms (Pure analog intensity modulation, speed of light).

metrics.rf: Tx: LC Tank / Crystal Osc + Antenna | Rx: Ferrite rod tuned circuit + AM Envelope Demodulator.
metrics.optical: Tx: High-Brightness LED Array + Current Driver | Rx: BPW34 PIN Photodiode + TIA Buffer.
